segments.t: What changed in the current release. The version this guide was built for is shown in the footer.

KTPH000AI memoryKTPH001 — korTTY keeps a memory that AI chat and the agent send with their requests: a global memory and one per connection, as plain Markdown files you can read and edit. It has a token budget per request, your own text is never changed without your confirmation, and the entries korTTY wrote can be merged, archived and restored from the archive (Show archive…); the history keeps earlier versions of a memory file that you can restore. See KTPH002AI memoryKTPH003.

KTPH000Reference files of other toolsKTPH001 — the CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and similar files of other AI tools can be added as read-only memory once you have read and approved their text; a changed file waits for your approval again. See KTPH002AI memoryKTPH003.

KTPH000Solution optionsKTPH001 — before a complex request runs, the agent can offer a recommended option, your own idea and an optional permanent rule. KTPH002Estimate complexityKTPH003 sets when this happens: Automatic, Always or Never. See KTPH004Solution optionsKTPH005.

KTPH000Rules learned from conversationsKTPH001 — in KTPH002Suggest rulesKTPH003 mode korTTY proposes a rule when a message says something should be kept for later; nothing is saved without your confirmation, and a saved rule can be undone for 30 seconds. Rules go into the memory or into a skill, and korTTY can create a new skill for a topic that has none. See KTPH004AI memoryKTPH005.
KTPH000Remember as rule…KTPH001 — saves a rule you write yourself, on your own chat messages and in the agent's prompt dialog, without an AI call.

KTPH000Sent alongKTPH001 — under each chat answer and each agent run, a collapsed line lists the memory entries, skills and reference files that were sent, masked as they were sent, with their token counts.

KTPH000Secret guardKTPH001 — korTTY refuses to save a password, key or token in a skill, a learned rule, the memory or an approved reference file, and it marks skills and memory notes that already hold one. The value is never shown. See KTPH002Secrets in skillsKTPH003.

KTPH000Skill statisticsKTPH001 — the KTPH002StatisticsKTPH003 dialog of AI Skills shows how often each skill is used, its size and its growth, with hints for skills to review. KTPH004Shorten...KTPH005 proposes a shorter version that is saved only after you confirm it. See KTPH006Skill statisticsKTPH007.

KTPH000Imported skill updatesKTPH001 — an update from the internet never overwrites a skill you changed; the update dialog then offers to import the provider's version as a copy or to skip that version. See KTPH002External skillsKTPH003.

KTPH002Enterprise policyKTPH003 — the KTPH000 table sets how the memory may be used, how rules are learned, whether korTTY may create skills, which reference files may be read, the token budget, the triage mode and the statistics. KTPH001 adds rules that every user gets and cannot change. See KTPH004Enterprise policyKTPH005.
KTPH000BackupsKTPH001 — the memory and the skill statistics are part of a backup. See KTPH002Backup KTPH004 restoreKTPH003.

KTPH004Kilo CLIKTPH005 — the Coding Agents panel now recognises KTPH006KiloKTPH007 (KTPH000 or KTPH001, npm package KTPH002), a fork of OpenCode: working, waiting for your answer and idle at its prompt. KTPH008RejectKTPH009 in its permission dialog first asks what Kilo should do differently, so the pane stays KTPH010waiting for youKTPH011 until you confirm with KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013. See KTPH014What it detectsKTPH015.

KTPH000Real compute backendKTPH001 — the KTPH002BackendKTPH003 column of the Runtimes and model tables shows the GPU or CPU backend a runtime computes on, as CPU, Metal, Vulkan or Auto: MLX runtimes and MLX models show Metal instead of "MLX", and before a runtime is installed the column shows the backend an installation would bring, such as "Metal (on install)". See KTPH004RuntimesKTPH005.
